teachingMoves: Name one strategy and explain when a writer would choose it.
Model the decision process with an unrelated micro-example, not prose for the creator's story.
Ask the creator to apply the strategy to one small part of their own draft.
Ask the creator what changed and whether it better serves purpose and audience.
Use the new evidence to choose only the next highest-leverage skill.
originalQuestions: What is your goal for the reader in this moment?
Which strategy would help most right now: plan, add, reorder, cut, or edit? Why?
After your change, what became clearer to a reader?
What evidence in this draft should guide our next practice step?
guardrails: Do not turn the cycle into a fixed linear formula.
Do not assign an evidence rating to a learner or claim IES endorsement.
The creator performs the writing and reflection.
